name: James Talarico
role: Texas state representative (2018–present); 2026 Democratic U.S. Senate nominee
summary: Talarico is a Texas legislator, former teacher and Christian seminarian who frames politics as a conflict between concentrated wealth and ordinary people. His legislative record includes abortion-access proposals and emissions-reduction targets; his interviews advocate universal health coverage, competitive markets, stronger public schools, church-state separation and support for Ukraine and NATO.

abortion-legal.rationale: He authored HJR 56 to limit the legislature’s ability to prohibit access to abortion care; its bill history identifies him as its author.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Rogan passage lists freedom to be an atheist, but does not address legal punishment for leaving a religion.

ban-cartels.rationale: His health-care platform calls for bipartisan antitrust legislation to break up vertically integrated health conglomerates and other health-care monopolies.

basic-income.rationale: At Rogan 57:27–58:54 he expresses interest in basic-income pilots and entrepreneurial grants while saying he does not know the best design; this is not an endorsement of an unconditional income for every adult.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The April 19, 2023 House Journal lists him among the nays on HB 900, which imposed sexual-content ratings and restrictions on school library books, in record vote 334.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: At CNN he says Netanyahu has no right to wage war against civilians, collectively punish them or restrict civilian aid.

clerical-rule.rationale: Called theocracy dangerous ("the only thing worse than a tyrant is a tyrant who thinks they are on a mission from God").

collective-bargaining.rationale: The sole cited source is an inaccessible campaign page; the earlier reference to the PRO Act alone does not specify how wages and conditions should be set.

collective-defense.rationale: At CNN he says Ukraine and NATO allies should be strengthened against Russian aggression so that the United States will not have to confront it elsewhere.

corporate-influence.rationale: At CNN he says big money has too much influence in politics and calls for banning both Democratic and Republican super PACs and corporate PACs.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The earlier rationale relies on an inaccessible campaign page and a report of court-reform views; changing court membership and ethics rules does not itself settle limits on majority power.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: At Rogan 16:58–21:26 he discusses the biblical prohibition and death penalty for same-sex relations and rejects importing those prohibitions into modern Christian politics.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The health-care page reports that he used a House procedural point of order to stop legislation removing people from Medicaid coverage.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The Tribune reports that his 2021 Texas Climate Action Act would require emissions cuts to 50 percent of 1990 levels by 2030 and 10 percent by 2050. Those legislative targets are the record on climate action.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: At CNN he explicitly calls for strengthening NATO allies against Russian aggression and describes support for Ukraine as a good investment.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: At Rogan 2:07–2:08 he says each person is of infinite worth, deserves unconditional love and should be treated as such in public policy.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The cited Rogan passage describes religious pluralism rather than the ethnic composition a nation should have.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The earlier answer relies solely on Wikipedia’s description of an energy plan; the CNN list of energy investments names wind, solar, geothermal, hydrogen and batteries.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The CNN proposals reverse tax breaks and close loopholes at the top, but do not specify an income-tax rate schedule.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The earlier rationale cites an inaccessible campaign page and Wikipedia’s account of support for the Equality Act, without an opened primary position on private discrimination.

god-not-male.rationale: The CNN interview says God cannot be defined using human categories, but does not advocate a rule about exclusively male language for God.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The earlier evidence criticises a Holocaust denier and uses the Holocaust as a historical reference; it does not set out Talarico’s own assessment of denial claims.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: At CNN he makes learning English a condition of the pathway to citizenship he proposes for long-established undocumented residents.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The earlier answer rests on an inaccessible campaign proposal; the opened health-care page and interviews do not set out an earned-income tax-credit policy.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: At CNN he says the economy should reward work instead of wealth and criticises a tax system that taxes work more heavily than wealth.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: In both his 2022 and 2024 ATPE survey responses he explicitly rejects replacing defined-benefit teacher pensions with contribution accounts that shift the savings risk to teachers.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The cited evidence defends Muslim students from exclusion; it does not address whether Islam is compatible with liberal democracy.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: At CNN he supports Israel’s security and a Palestinian state, but does not discuss the Jewish people’s right to a state in the Land of Israel as such.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Called theocracy the most dangerous form of government and Christian nationalism the worship of power; opposes using law to impose a religion.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Told Rogan he thinks of politics less as left versus right and more top versus bottom, and works across the aisle.

legalize-drugs.rationale: His public-safety platform calls specifically for regulated adult marijuana sales and expungement of marijuana records; it does not settle the legal status of recreational drugs generally.

limit-guns.rationale: His public-safety platform would require universal background checks and secure storage around children and raise the purchase age for specified semi-automatic rifles.

more-religion-public.rationale: On Rogan at 2:15:46 he calls for faith leaders to recover their public moral voice and says that clarity is missing from politics, while opposing state-imposed religion.

national-church-status.rationale: Said America is a nation where no religion is elevated over the others and criticized using state power to elevate one tradition.

no-business-privileges.rationale: At CNN he condemns politicians granting sweetheart tax deals to data-centre companies that finance them and calls for ending that corruption.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: At CNN he calls for a two-state solution securing Israel and Palestinian self-determination, rather than retaining all disputed territory.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: At Rogan 10:30–11:43 he rejects the government taking the place of pastors and Sunday-school teachers and says religious teaching belongs in houses of worship.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Said wealthy lawmakers should widen their circle of concern to neighbors in other cities, citing FDR and Bobby Kennedy.

open-borders.rationale: The CNN border-security plan addresses present enforcement and legal pathways, not whether borders should eventually be open.

party-controls-media.rationale: The earlier rationale relies on an inaccessible free-press pledge; the Rogan criticism of platform algorithms does not state whether the state should control media.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: At CNN he explicitly promises to oppose his own party when its decisions conflict with Texans’ interests and says party membership is neither his religion nor his sports team.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: At Rogan he says patriotism can be reclaimed, but does not join that claim to a stated doctrine that patriotism and working-class politics belong together.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: At CNN he describes politicians in both parties as bought by corporate interests and billionaire donors who rig economic rules for their benefit.

prohibit-child-medical-transition.rationale: The May 15, 2023 House Journal records his vote against SB 14 and his proposed sunset if high-quality studies establish the safety and efficacy of treatment; this opposes a blanket statutory ban.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The cited Rogan passage defends religious freedom and rejects state-imposed Christianity; it does not discuss civil penalties for blasphemy or false religion.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: At the CNN town hall he calls for raising the minimum wage in response to a voter describing the $7.25 rate.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Describes faith as the foundation he falls back on and as essential to meaning, not reason alone.

reduce-immigration.rationale: At CNN he calls for more legal immigration pathways alongside border enforcement; this does not specify an overall immigration level.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The health-care page’s legislative record reports insulin price-gouging controls, surprise-billing protections and regulation of anticompetitive insurance consolidation.

rehabilitation.rationale: The earlier evidence concerns diplomas for incarcerated minors and particular reentry programmes, which can coexist with a prison system primarily organised around punishment.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: At Rogan 18:10–19:22 he rejects applying ancient legal prohibitions directly in the modern setting and instead makes love of neighbour the governing Christian standard.

religion-illusion.rationale: At Rogan 2:10–2:12 he describes humans as an inherently believing species and argues that losing religious community leaves people without a framework for meaning.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: At Rogan 13:06–15:20 he recognises religious control of women while arguing that this violates Christian teaching; at 23:15 he describes Jesus’ affirmation of women as equals.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The Rogan interview describes overlapping ethics and patterns across religions, which is a narrower claim than all authentic religions expressing one underlying truth.

religious-nation.rationale: Said the country was not founded as a Christian nation but as one where people may be Christian, Jewish, Muslim, Sikh, Buddhist or atheist.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Says he evaluates policy by whether it helps his students, not by party.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The earlier answer relies on a refused campaign page about USAID; the opened CNN discussion is about strategic support for Ukraine rather than a duty to aid the world’s poor.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The earlier answer rests on an inaccessible campaign pledge and on loving gay neighbours in the Rogan interview; that interview passage does not address marriage law.

school-vouchers.rationale: The April 16, 2025 House Journal lists him among the nays on SB 2, the education-savings-account voucher bill, in record vote 286.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: At Rogan 16:32–19:22 he challenges a literal application of ancient scriptural prohibitions and rejects legalism in favour of Jesus’ commandments to love God and neighbour.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Javier Ambler’s Law restricts reality-TV police contracts; that reform does not itself establish legal accountability of governments for past killings or abuses.

separate-church-state.rationale: At Rogan 1:06–2:22 he defends the boundary between church and state as essential to religious coexistence and explicitly opposes attempts to erode it.

separated-powers.rationale: The sole cited campaign page on checks and balances refused access; the opened interviews discuss corruption and elections without stating this institutional arrangement.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The earlier answer uses an excerpt reporting two sexes and correcting a count of sexes; that does not by itself answer whether sex categories are socially constructed.

social-market-economy.rationale: At CNN he advocates competitive capitalism with antitrust enforcement and shared growth, alongside guaranteed health coverage and investment in public schools.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Told Rogan the coming AI disruption is first of all a spiritual problem and that people need community to wrestle with ultimate questions.

state-harmful.rationale: The earlier rationale cites seeking office and supporting particular public programmes; those activities do not state a judgment on whether the state itself is unnecessary and harmful.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Rogan interview opposes government religious instruction; it does not address state promotion of atheism.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The earlier rationale attributes the debt-relief claim to Rogan rather than to a clear answer from Talarico himself.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The earlier answer concerns repealing particular Trump tariffs, which does not settle whether tariffs should protect domestic industry in general; its campaign sources refused access.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: At the CNN town hall he advocates reversing the $3 trillion in tax cuts for the top one percent and closing billionaire tax loopholes to reduce the deficit.

term-limits.rationale: At CNN he calls for term limits to remove career politicians and prevent officeholding from becoming a project of self-preservation.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The earlier rationale mentions worker protections but does not establish environmental standards as a condition of trade agreements; both cited campaign pages refused access.

unions-good.rationale: In his full ATPE candidate survey he calls unions advocates for educators and strongly encourages all educators to join a union or professional association.

universal-healthcare.rationale: On Rogan at 2:08, Talarico says he fights for universal healthcare; his health-care page proposes a Medicare option open to every American.

voter-id.rationale: In both the Rogan and CNN interviews he supports fair voter identification but objects to selective ID rules; neither passage settles the additional requirement to show proof of citizenship.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: At CNN he says billionaire donors buy politicians, rig economic rules and distort elections through unlimited secret campaign money.

notes: Later pass checked every statement, including candidates. Searched economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means and globalism in the full Rogan and CNN interviews and retrieved legislative material. The MediaSum corpus returned zero Talarico transcripts; the local reference library has no book by him, and US Congress/foreign-parliament corpora do not cover a Texas state representative. Campaign pages s4–s11 and The Reload s13 returned HTTP 403 and were not retried; GitHub repository/code searches found no mirror. The tech issue page also returned 403. Sources s2 and the blocked pages survive only to document earlier versions. Source s17a refers only to the record section of the same page as words source s17. The CNN town hall clarifies several earlier claims; recent words do not replace legislative actions. Follow-up searches addressed secession, territorial autonomy, minority-language provision, supranational institutions and executive checks. They did not yield additional qualifying positions on those statements. A Diary of a CEO transcript also returned HTTP 403 and was not retried. ATPE’s complete 2022/2024 survey responses were read as primary words, and the linked House Journals were checked for voucher and library-book votes. These vote documents replace interview claims wherever they settle the same statement. No further qualifying evidence was found for the remaining thin themes. Source s3a separately identifies the health-care page’s report of legislative actions; those reported actions, at medium confidence, replace campaign promises on corporate regulation and welfare cuts. The AP election-result page also refused access with HTTP 403.
